newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - public pay awards have to be staggered.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - public pay awards have to be staggered.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday he had to make the 3.3 percent public pay award in two stages in order to afford it, and to strike the right balance between public services and rewards to staff.

"We have to stage it to make sure it's affordable. You have to get the balance right between the public services we want and rewarding the key staff who work so hard to deliver them," he told Sky Television in an interview.
The government said earlier on Thursday it would raise the pay of about 1.3 million public sector workers by an average 3.3 percent, payable in two stages.

Prime Minister John Major said in a written parliamentary answer that a first-stage payment of two percent would be made on April 1 with the balance of the recommended increases to be paid from December 1.
